questions.question_text: The mean and standard deviation of $100$ items are $50$ and $4$ , respectively then the sum of all squares of the items is
questions.question_html: The mean and standard deviation of $100$ items are $50$ and $4$ , respectively then the sum of all squares of the items is
questions.explanation_text: For $100$ items, the mean is $\bar{x}=50$ and the standard deviation is $\sigma=4$ . Using the formula $\sigma^{2}=\frac{\sum x_{i}^{2}}{n}-\bar{x}^{2}$ Substitute the given values: $4^{2}=\frac{\sum x_{i}^{2}}{100}-50^{2}$ $16=\frac{\sum x_{i}^{2}}{100}-2500$ So, $\frac{\sum x_{i}^{2}}{100}=2516$ $\sum x_{i}^{2}=2516 \times 100=251600$ Hence, the sum of all squares of the items is $251600$ Correct option: Option B.
questions.explanation_html:
For $100$ items, the mean is $\bar{x}=50$ and the standard deviation is $\sigma=4$ .

Using the formula

$\sigma^{2}=\frac{\sum x_{i}^{2}}{n}-\bar{x}^{2}$

Substitute the given values:

$4^{2}=\frac{\sum x_{i}^{2}}{100}-50^{2}$

$16=\frac{\sum x_{i}^{2}}{100}-2500$

So,

$\frac{\sum x_{i}^{2}}{100}=2516$

$\sum x_{i}^{2}=2516 \times 100=251600$

Hence, the sum of all squares of the items is

$251600$

Correct option: Option B.

questions.question_html: Let $a,b,c,d$ and $e$ be the observations with mean $m$ and standard deviation $S$ . The standard deviation of the observations $a+k$ , $b+k,c+k,d+k$ and $e+k$ is
questions.explanation_text: $\begin{aligned} & \text{The given observation are}a,b,c,d\text{and}e \\ & \begin{aligned} & \text{Mean}=m=\frac{a+b+c+d+e}{5} \\ & \Rightarrow \Sigma x_{i}=a+b+c+d+e=5m \\ & \therefore \text{Standard deviation,}S=\sqrt{\frac{\Sigma x_{i}^{2}}{5}-m^{2}} \end{aligned} \end{aligned}$ Now, consider the observations $a+k,b+k,c+k$ , $d+k,e+k$ . Now, mean $\begin{aligned} & \text{mean} \\ & =\frac{(a+k)+(b+k)+(c+k)+(d+k)+(e+k)}{5} \\ & =\frac{a+b+c+d+e+5k}{5} \\ & =\frac{5m+5k}{5}=m+k \end{aligned}$ $\begin{aligned} & \therefore \text{New standard devaition}=\sqrt{\frac{\sum (x_{i}+k)^{2}}{5}-(m+k)^{2}} \\ & \\ & =\sqrt{\frac{\sum (x_{i}^{2}+k^{2}+2x_{i}k)}{5}-(m^{2}+k^{2}+2mk)} \\ & \\ & =\sqrt{\frac{\sum x_{i}^{2}}{5}-m^{2}+\frac{5k^{2}}{5}-k^{2}+\frac{2k\Sigma x_{i}}{5}-2mk} \\ & \\ & =\sqrt{\frac{\sum x_{i}^{2}}{5}-m^{2}+\frac{2k \times 5m}{5}-2mk} \\ & \\ & =\sqrt{\frac{\sum x_{i}^{2}}{5}-m^{2}}=S \end{aligned}$

questions.question_text: If the standard deviation of the numbers $-1,0,1,k$ is $\sqrt{5}$ where $k>0$ , then $k$ is equal to
questions.question_html: If the standard deviation of the numbers $-1,0,1,k$ is $\sqrt{5}$ where $k>0$ , then $k$ is equal to
questions.explanation_text: Given, numbers are $-1,0,1,k$ . Standard deviation, $\sigma=\sqrt{5}$ $\sigma^{2}=\frac{\Sigma x_{i}^{2}}{n}-(\frac{\Sigma x_{i}}{n})^{2}$ $\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 5=\frac{1+0+1+k^{2}}{4}-(\frac{-1+0+1+k}{4})^{2} \\ & \Rightarrow 5=\frac{2+k^{2}}{4}-\frac{k^{2}}{16} \Rightarrow 80=8+4k^{2}-k^{2} \\ & \Rightarrow 72=3k^{2} \Rightarrow k^{2}=24 \Rightarrow k=2\sqrt{6} \end{aligned}$
questions.explanation_html:
Given, numbers are $-1,0,1,k$ .

Standard deviation, $\sigma=\sqrt{5}$

$\sigma^{2}=\frac{\Sigma x_{i}^{2}}{n}-(\frac{\Sigma x_{i}}{n})^{2}$

$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 5=\frac{1+0+1+k^{2}}{4}-(\frac{-1+0+1+k}{4})^{2} \\ & \Rightarrow 5=\frac{2+k^{2}}{4}-\frac{k^{2}}{16} \Rightarrow 80=8+4k^{2}-k^{2} \\ & \Rightarrow 72=3k^{2} \Rightarrow k^{2}=24 \Rightarrow k=2\sqrt{6} \end{aligned}$

questions.question_html: The standard deviation of the numbers $31,32,33\dots46,47$ is
questions.explanation_text: Given, numbers : $31,32,33,\dots,46,47$ . The standard deviation of $31,32,33,\dots,47$ will be the same as those of $1,2,3,\dots,17$ . (decreasing each item by 30) $\because SD=\sqrt{\frac{n^{2}-1}{12}}$ Here, $n=17$ $\begin{aligned} \therefore SD & =\sqrt{\frac{17^{2}-1}{12}}=\sqrt{\frac{288}{12}} \\ & =\sqrt{24}=2\sqrt{6} \end{aligned}$
questions.explanation_html:
Given, numbers : $31,32,33,\dots,46,47$ .

The standard deviation of $31,32,33,\dots,47$ will be the same as those of $1,2,3,\dots,17$ . (decreasing each item by 30)

$\because SD=\sqrt{\frac{n^{2}-1}{12}}$

Here, $n=17$

$\begin{aligned} \therefore SD & =\sqrt{\frac{17^{2}-1}{12}}=\sqrt{\frac{288}{12}} \\ & =\sqrt{24}=2\sqrt{6} \end{aligned}$

questions.question_text: The standard deviation of the data 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 is
questions.question_html: The standard deviation of the data 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 is
questions.explanation_html:
Given data $6,7,8,9,10$

$\begin{aligned} \bar{x} & =\frac{6+7+8+9+10}{5}=8 \\ SD & =\sqrt{\frac{\Sigma x_{i}^{2}}{n}-(\bar{x})^{2}} \\ SD & =\sqrt{\frac{6^{2}+7^{2}+8^{2}+9^{2}+10^{2}}{5}-(8)^{2}} \\ SD & =\sqrt{\frac{36+49+64+81+100-320}{5}} \\ SD & =\sqrt{\frac{330-320}{5}}=\sqrt{\frac{10}{5}}=\sqrt{2} \end{aligned}$

questions.question_html: Mean and standard deviation of 100 items are 50 and 4 , respectively. The sum of all squares of the items is
questions.explanation_text: Key Idea Use mean $(\bar{x})=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n}x_{i}}{n}$ and standard deviation (S.D) $=\sqrt{⎷\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n}xi^{2}}{n}-⎛⎝⎜\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n}xi}{n}⎞⎠⎟^{2}}$ $\begin{aligned} & \text{Given,}\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{100}xi}{100}=50 \\ & \begin{aligned} & \text{and}=\sqrt{⎷\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{100}xi^{2}}{100}-⎛⎝⎜\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{100}xi}{100}⎞⎠⎟^{2}}=4 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{100}xi^{2}}{100}-(50)^{2}=(4)^{2} \Rightarrow \sum_{i=1}^{100}xi^{2}=100(2500+16) \\ & =251600 \end{aligned} \end{aligned}$

questions.question_text: If coefficient of variation is 60 and standard deviation is 24 , then Arithmetic mean is
questions.question_html: If coefficient of variation is 60 and standard deviation is 24 , then Arithmetic mean is
questions.explanation_text: We are given: Coefficient of Variation (CV) = 60 Standard Deviation ( $\sigma$ ) = 24 To find the Arithmetic Mean ( $\bar{x}$ ), we use the formula for the Coefficient of Variation: $CV=\frac{\sigma}{\bar{x}} \times 100$ Substituting the given values: $60=\frac{24}{\bar{x}} \times 100$ To solve for $\bar{x}$ , rearrange the equation: $\bar{x}=\frac{24 \times 100}{60}$ Simplifying the expression: $\bar{x}=40$ Therefore, the Arithmetic Mean is 40.
questions.explanation_html:
We are given:

Coefficient of Variation (CV) = 60

Standard Deviation ( $\sigma$ ) = 24

To find the Arithmetic Mean ( $\bar{x}$ ), we use the formula for the Coefficient of Variation:

$CV=\frac{\sigma}{\bar{x}} \times 100$

Substituting the given values:

$60=\frac{24}{\bar{x}} \times 100$

To solve for $\bar{x}$ , rearrange the equation:

$\bar{x}=\frac{24 \times 100}{60}$

Simplifying the expression:

$\bar{x}=40$

Therefore, the Arithmetic Mean is 40.
